query: Of Your Own Strength Pell closes the shop early, sets the old still on the bench and holds the lamp himself. "Brew it," he says. "I'll count." The recipe card lies beside you. {flag(distil_drops) and flag(distil_moonwort) and flag(distil_shortcut): You know every step of it.|There are steps you haven't practised.} Brew the draught The draught comes down to one shining drop, and as it falls you feel exactly what it took from you, and how to take it again. Pell stops counting. "Fair," he says, twice in one year. The mixture boils over and takes more out of you than it should. Pell puts the card back in the drawer and writes "Don't." on the front. Next term, perhaps. Use Pell's own moonwort stock With the good stock, it comes down clean to one drop. You feel it pull, and you feel where it pulls from. Pell writes the cost in his ledger, and your name beside the recipe. Even with his best stock it boils over. Pell writes "Don't." on the drawer and the cost in the ledger. Next term, perhaps.
